failure_modes.title: The scoring tool does not simulate the shipped decision, so every published merge number is wrong
failure_modes.mechanism_short: The evaluation script decides a merge with one threshold test per log line. The real system requires the same pair to pass the threshold on two scoring sweeps in a row, and it counts pairs, not lines. So the script reports merges that the system could never have made.
failure_modes.size: MEASURED. On run 20260914_180343: 16 reported merges across 5 options fall to 1 when each pair is replayed through the real decision class (denominator 20 ground-truth duplicate pairs); recall 0.15/0.15/0.15/0.25/0.10 falls to 0.00/0.00/0.00/0.05/0.00. On run 20260914_174342: 13 reported merges fall to 0 (denominator 6 ground-truth pairs), and that bundle's option ranking is the inverse of the other bundle's. 15 of 16 reported merges (94%) are unreachable; line-vs-pair double counting explains only 1 of the 16.
failure_modes.fix_short: Delete the copied decision logic in /DATA/GRAPH-API/.claude/worktrees/found-merge-algorithm/.handoff/lanes/merge-algorithm/verify/attr_options_gt.py:113-181 and import the real classes (association.Hypothesis, association.PairScore); group rows by pair, replay in sweep order, read merge_min_consecutive and merge_min_evidence from config.yaml instead of literals. Add one additive telemetry key (measured_abstentions) to the refusal row so the replay can tell an abstention from a missing channel. Evaluator-only; the robot's behaviour does not change.
failure_modes.citations: verify/attr_options_gt.py:160 (bare threshold), :161-177 (row counting), :82-111 (class-agnostic many-to-one GT assignment); association.py:1165-1215 (Hypothesis.decide); object_services.py:2110-2112 (the real call)

failure_modes.title: Every channel that measures its own scale from the run's data gets a scale of zero, and the code substitutes a floor for the missing measurement
failure_modes.mechanism_short: To judge whether two boxes are far apart, the code needs to know how uncertain each position is. It estimates that from the spread of the object's past sightings, but every sighting of one object stores the same single point, so the spread is exactly zero. The function then returns a near-zero uncertainty instead of saying 'not measurable', which turns a 1.15 m gap into an 18,000-sigma disagreement and emits the maximum negative score on every non-touching pair.
failure_modes.size: MEASURED, two runs (20260914_174342, 20260914_180343), 139 refusal rows of which 97 carry channel values. Separation channel: 41 of 41 scored rows at exactly -8.0 (the floor). Implied covariance exactly 4.000e-9 on 39 of 41 rows and 3.500e-9 on 2 — the exact output of the zero-spread branch. Appearance channel: 3 of 3 rows at -8.0, because its scale is a mean of per-component deviations where the distance it divides is a full-vector norm (a factor sqrt(512) = 22.6 too small). Tracking reach: the uncertainty term contributes 0.15 mm instead of the 1.0 m fallback, on 63 of 139 object visits. On GA-493 geometry, restoring the fallback moves reachable ordered pairs from 532 to 1,408 of 10,712 (same-label 174 to 336 of 824).
failure_modes.fix_short: Four edits. (1) association.py:233-242 — return None when nothing measured the position, instead of a 1e-9 floor; all three consumers already have a written 'unmeasurable' path. (2) object_manager_6.py:1548 — record each sighting at this frame's own box centre, not the object's frozen creation centroid. (3) delete the stale centroid override at object_services.py:1659 and object_manager_6.py:181. (4) association.py:1279 — use the vector norm of the per-component deviations, not their mean. No sensor constant is guessed: depth_sparsity and pose_sigma_m stay unpassed on purpose. The repair itself ships; the 1.0 m tracking fallback it revives (object_manager_6.py:145, never measured, absent from config.yaml) must be swept at 0.3/0.5/1.0/1.5 m in the one experiment, recording association recall AND duplicate-add count with both denominators.
failure_modes.citations: association.py:218-246 (position_covariance and its own docstring forbidding the floor), :437-470 (channel_separation), :687-688 (appearance distance vs scale), :987-990 (search_radius); object_info.py:20 (the only write of Object.centroid); object_manager_6.py:145, :180-185, :1547-1555

failure_modes.title: The attribute channel measures the object's class, not which object it is, and on same-kind pairs it can only vote yes
failure_modes.mechanism_short: The attribute score is 85% of its weight in three string comparisons (label, colour, material) drawn from a tiny vocabulary — 33 labels, 11 colours, 8 materials over 104 objects. When two objects share all three, the score sits exactly at or above the reference by construction, so the channel's negative branch is unreachable and it always argues for merging. A pair whose descriptions cannot even be compared scores 1.0 and receives the largest possible vote.
failure_modes.size: MEASURED on the GA-493 final map (104 objects) and the two 2026-09-14 runs. As an instance discriminator the score reaches AUC 0.5324 (geometry proxy, 43 positives x 312 known-different same-label pairs), 0.5127 (ground truth, 40 x 285) and 0.3461 (ground truth with an IoU floor of 0.1, 17 x 60 — below chance). 249 of 312 known-different same-label pairs currently vote FOR the merge at a median +1.13 nats, 37.8% of the commit threshold; 0 of 312 receive a negative value. Bounded cost of muting it: the verdict flips on 1 of 38 non-vetoed scored pairs in one run and 2 of 18 in the other.
failure_modes.fix_short: In association.py:756-807 move the same_kind test to the front of the branch cascade so it catches the positive arm as well as the negative one, returning 0.0 (not an abstention, which would blank the containment guard at association.py:1198). Add one telemetry key same_kind_muted. The cross-kind negative arm is untouched. No constant is introduced.
failure_modes.citations: association.py:756-807 (channel_attributes), :781-788 (the branch order), :857 (evidence_count ignores a 0.0), :1198 (containment guard); config.yaml:46-48 (label 0.25 + colour 0.36 + material 0.24 = 0.85); object_services.py:1632 (reference = sim_threshold)

failure_modes.title: A veto fired once is remembered forever inside one hypothesis, while the garbage collector deletes the same veto for any pair not re-offered
failure_modes.mechanism_short: If two objects appear in the same camera frame but their 2D boxes barely overlap, the code vetoes the pair — correctly, they are two things seen at once. But the veto is appended to a list that is never cleared, so a later sweep that sees them overlapping cannot lift it. Meanwhile a separate cleanup step deletes the whole record for any pair not re-offered, so whether the veto is permanent is decided by luck.
failure_modes.size: MEASURED. The veto fires on 41 of 97 evidence-engine scored rows (42.3%) across the two runs, covering 37 of 116 distinct offered pairs; all 41 on one shared frame with 2D overlap below 0.30 (exactly 0.0 on 17, between 0.0022 and 0.1455 on 24). Effect on outcomes today: 0 of 41 — summing the other channels on the same sweep, none reaches the 2.9957 commit threshold (maximum 2.60) and none is a same-label pair. The population this repairs (a pair whose overlap crosses 0.30 on a later sweep) has size 0 in every bundle on disk, because no bundle has enough sweeps.
failure_modes.fix_short: In association.py:1118-1127 replace the veto list each sweep instead of appending to it, exactly as the same method already does for every other channel three lines below. The veto still wins on the sweep it fires (total stays -inf, decide still answers reject) and still breaks the streak. Add one key, total_if_unvetoed, to the refusal record (association.py:903-910) so the counterfactual both reviewers had to rebuild by hand becomes a column. Watch one newly exposed path: sightings are a capped queue of 64, so forgetting the frame that produced a veto can now lift it.
failure_modes.citations: association.py:479-568 (channel_covisibility), :1113 (total = -inf while vetoed), :1118-1127 (the append), :1136-1141 (the replace rule it violates), :1184 (decide); object_services.py:1568-1578 (the garbage collector that erases it)

failure_modes.title: A merge throws away the discarded object's sightings, leaves the survivor's centre frozen, and labels the new box 'keeper' when it is the union of both
failure_modes.mechanism_short: When two map objects are merged, the survivor gets a box enclosing both, but the record says the box came from the survivor alone. The survivor also never inherits the other object's sightings, and its stored centre point is never rewritten, so it stays where the object was first created. The move path in the same file already copies sightings correctly; the merge path simply does not.
failure_modes.size: CODE-LEVEL AND UNCONDITIONAL on every applied merge: the union write, the false label and the dropped sightings all fire 100% of the time. NO RUN ON DISK EXERCISES IT: all five local bundles applied 0 merges, and the only bundle with merges (GA-493, 15 of them) ran an older source where the survivor kept its own box — measured, kept volume equals volume A in 15 of 15. Replaying those 15 through the current block grows the survivor's box in 14 of 15, lower-bound factor median x1.75, p90 x15.4, max x41.9 (denominator 15). The falsifier is not runnable: the 15 merge rows carry 10 keys and none of them is merged_bbox.
failure_modes.fix_short: One 8-line helper in object_services.py after :378 plus one call inside the locked apply block before :2444: the survivor inherits the discard's sightings (deduplicated on frame id, capped at the existing association.max_observations_per_object = 64) and takes the hull's centre. Change the record's bbox_source value from "keeper" to "union_hull" (object_services.py:2357) — no code reads it, so this corrects a wrong value, not a key's meaning. Do NOT revert the union write: the ordinary update path unions the same way and no path in the tree shrinks a box. No constant is chosen; the sightings half must be counted before/after on the first run that actually applies a merge.
failure_modes.citations: object_services.py:354-378 (_combine_object_geometry), :2357-2358 (the false label), :2417-2470 (the locked apply block), :2438-2440 (the hull write), :2444 (remove, the last reference to the discard), :2988-2993 (the move path, which copies sightings); object_info.py:20 (the only write of centroid); git blame: label af1011ca 2026-09-01, hull write 2b82862 2026-09-14

failure_modes.title: The two-sweeps-in-a-row rule is priced in a unit the run stops producing exactly when a merge is pending
failure_modes.mechanism_short: A merge commits only if the same pair passes the threshold on two scoring sweeps in a row. A sweep runs only when the robot completes a full 360-degree turn, and the periodic timer that would sweep while standing still is off because the config file has no merge section at all. Every pair that ever passed the threshold did so on the run's last sweep, after which the robot stood still for 90 seconds and no second sweep existed.
failure_modes.size: MEASURED, two runs. 3 of 3 verdicts that crossed the threshold were refused for the streak alone; 0 merges committed over 116 distinct pairs. 104 of 116 pairs (89.7%) never received a second scored update; in run 20260914_174342 that is 61 of 61 pairs. The precision this rule buys is not measured at zero — it is unmeasurable, denominator 0, because no pair was ever scored above the threshold on a sweep that had a successor. Headroom is capped elsewhere: 41 of 41 non-touching pairs are floored by the separation channel and 33 pairs are refused before scoring, so 74 of 116 cannot reach the streak at all.
failure_modes.fix_short: Two edits that do not work apart: add a merge.periodic_interval_s key to config.yaml (the reader, timer and lock already exist at object_manager_6.py:317, :957-959, :1250-1273) and change the streak to count re-MEASUREMENTS rather than repeats of one unchanged score, recording a streak_fresh flag. Ship the interval at 0.0 (off). BEHIND MEASUREMENT: run one bundle at three interval values from the environment and read the fresh fraction — the share of above-threshold offers that carried changed evidence — then set the smallest interval whose fresh fraction stays high. Do NOT change merge_min_consecutive in this fix; this fix is what creates the denominator for that question.
failure_modes.citations: config.yaml:84 (merge_min_consecutive = 2), config.yaml has no merge: block; object_manager_6.py:316-318 (TIAGO_MERGE_INTERVAL_S defaults 0.0), :957-959 (timer created only when positive), :1191 (a repeated scan id is refused); association.py:1208-1215 (streak increment and reset); habitat_feed_host.py:1000 (the 90 s end-of-run settle, which turns nothing)

failure_modes.title: With every other channel silent or capped, the commit threshold is a threshold on the box-overlap channel alone
failure_modes.mechanism_short: Six of the seven evidence channels can never push a merge over the line: two are switched off, one has no code path that returns a positive number, two only ever return their maximum negative value, and the attribute one is capped at 2.0 against a threshold of 2.9957. So in practice the decision is made by box overlap alone, and objects with near-flat boxes (rug, mirror, picture) have no route to a merge at all.
failure_modes.size: MEASURED, denominator 97 scored merge rows from two runs of one single-room scene. Removing the overlap channel, 0 of 97 rows reach 2.9957; the largest remainder is 1.517 nats. Summing only the positive non-overlap channels, the maximum is exactly 2.000 nats (the configured attribute cap) on 0 of 97 rows. Channel participation: overlap 97 (53 positive), attributes 97 (10 positive), separation 41 (all -8.0), appearance 3 (all -8.0), covisibility 0, ontology 0, room 0. Flat objects: 11 of 104 in GA-493 have near-zero box volume, so overlap abstains on them.
failure_modes.fix_short: Give the co-visibility channel the positive branch it already has the measurement for: it computes the best 2D overlap in a shared frame and throws the number away. Add one config key merge_covisibility_max_log_odds, ship it at 0.0 so behaviour is byte-identical, and use a ramp from the 0.30 veto boundary up to the cap (association.py:479, :549-554). BEHIND MEASUREMENT: the cap must be fitted from ground truth — the two 2D-overlap distributions for same-object and different-object pairs — before it leaves 0.0. It also depends on the self-scale repair; until then nothing can reach the threshold anyway.
failure_modes.citations: association.py:137-170 (shared_frame_overlap_2d, the measurement already taken), :479-568 (every return is an abstention or a veto), :415-431 (channel_overlap ceiling log(V_map/V_larger)); config.yaml:77 (ontology off), :78 (attribute cap 2.0), :82-84 (cost ratio 20, min_consecutive 2); object_services.py:1594-1600 (V_map)

failure_modes.title: The candidate list is handed to the matcher in database index order, so which object absorbs a detection is arbitrary
failure_modes.mechanism_short: Geometry decides which existing objects are even considered for a new detection — that part is confirmed and correct. But the list comes back in spatial-index order, which is arbitrary, and the first candidate over the score bar wins. The distance that the gate already computed is thrown away instead of being used to rank.
failure_modes.size: MEASURED on the GA-493 replay, denominator 119 add calls. Geometry is the binding refusal on 66 of 119 adds; 42 associated. 18 of 119 adds had two or more candidates over the score bar, and the score-based pick differed from the nearest box on 8 of them; only 2 of those 8 have a non-zero distance difference and would actually flip. So the predicted change is 2 of 119 adds. The gate's WIDTH is refuted as a cause: 58 of 59 ground-truth re-observation adds already had their partner within 0.3 m (median 0.000 m, p90 0.09 m), and the gate refused 1 of 59.
failure_modes.fix_short: Sort the candidate list by box gap, nearest first, in _association_candidates (object_manager_6.py:219-228) — the single function both candidate loops route through. Do NOT widen association_margin_m from 0.3 (config.yaml:63): the data lens refuted that, and the far same-label neighbours are different instances of one kind (gap distribution is bimodal, median 0.10 m against p90 4.02 m). The same-cycle veto must not be touched in the same change; it is what stops a wider gate fusing two adjacent pillows.
failure_modes.citations: object_manager_6.py:219-228 (_association_candidates, one caller at :1822), :1874 and :1977 (the two locality gates), :1911 and :1951 (first-over-the-bar wins, then break), :2009 (tracking argmax); association.py:325 (box_gap), :353-370 (locality_box); world_model.py:269 (rtree index order); verify/assoc_argmax_probe.out

failure_modes.title: The pending-merge file is written before the sweep scores anything, so it always describes the previous sweep
failure_modes.mechanism_short: A small status file reports how many pairs are one sweep short of committing. It is written as the last statement before the scoring loop starts, so it always reports the previous sweep's state, and the final sweep of a run is never published at all. The consumer that reads the number never ran in any recorded run, so nothing was actually lost.
failure_modes.size: MEASURED. 4 of 4 local bundles that carry the file publish a one-sweep-stale blob, all reporting pending 0 and needs_max 0; in 2 of 2 bundles that also recorded merge decisions the file's timestamp precedes the sweep's first merge row (by 0.023 s and 0.0034 s). Pairs hidden: 3, in 1 of 4 bundles (run 20260914_180343 sweep 4, at 3.579 / 4.314 / 5.400 log-odds, each 1 of 2 consecutive). Merges lost by this route: 0 of 5 local bundles — 5 of 5 run_metadata.json say multi_floor false, so the only consumer branch was unreachable, and 0 of 5 feed_stats.json carry its output keys.
failure_modes.fix_short: Move one statement: delete the publish call at object_services.py:1829 and put the same call in _cb_merge_objects after the per-pair scoring loop, before the response block (around :2514). No key changes meaning, the lock state is identical. Newly exposed: in multi-floor runs a truthful non-zero count can stall the floor drain, because no sweep can run during the 90 s settle — that path has never been observed.
failure_modes.citations: object_services.py:1829 (the only publish site, last statement of _merge_candidates), :1974 (scoring loop starts), :2514 (the anchor for the new site); habitat_feed_host.py:2205-2252 (the settle), :2236-2244 (multi-floor drain break), :2672-2676 (the keys absent from every bundle)

plan.headline: The dominant failure mode is self-scale collapse: every channel that derives its own scale from the run's own data derives it from data with no variation, the code substitutes a floor for the missing measurement, and what survives is a merge decision made by one channel — but nothing here can be scored until the evaluation tool stops simulating a decision the system does not make.
plan.one_experiment: ONE replay of the GA-493 bundle (plus one fresh run long enough to produce at least five scoring sweeps), with the four correctness repairs applied (self-scale E1-E4, attribute mute, co-visibility re-measure, merge survivor absorb), scored ONLY by the repaired instrument, sweeping merge.periodic_interval_s over three values from the environment and TRACKING_FALLBACK_RADIUS_M over 0.3 / 0.5 / 1.0 / 1.5 m, and recording per run: association recall AND duplicate-add count with both denominators; the separation channel's abstention rate against its former 41-of-41 floor; the fresh fraction of above-threshold offers (streak_fresh); the number of pairs reaching a second scored sweep; total_if_unvetoed on every vetoed row; the count of applied merges plus the co-visibility-terminated refusals and the appearance channel's first non-abstaining rows; and the survivor's sighting counts before and after each applied merge. That single run settles, at once: whether the separation repair changes any merge (currently 0 of 14 eligible rows, sample too small); the tracking fallback value, which is unmeasured and 1.0 m by an owner ruling; the periodic interval, which has no measured value; whether merge_min_consecutive = 2 has any denominator at all (today it is 0, so its precision is unmeasurable, not zero); whether the appearance and co-visibility channels can ever return a positive number in a live decision; and whether the merge apply block corrupts the survivor, which no bundle on disk can show because 0 merges were applied under the current source.
plan.order:
STEP 0, BEFORE ANY OTHER MEASUREMENT — instrument-overstates-and-misattributes. It is evaluator-only, zero production risk, and it is a CORRECTNESS REPAIR. Until it lands, every number any later fix is judged by is wrong by 15 of 16 on one bundle and by 13 of 13 on the other, and the two bundles rank the options in opposite directions. Nothing else may be ranked first.

STEP 1 — the CORRECTNESS REPAIRS, in this order, each landing on its own self-check with no new data required:
 1a. self-scale-collapse. Largest measured mechanism (41 of 41 separation rows at the -8.0 floor, 3 of 3 appearance rows, tracking reach 0.15 mm instead of 1.0 m). Independent of every other fix. It must land BEFORE the co-visibility positive cap, because until it lands nothing can reach the threshold anyway.
 1b. attributes-cannot-discriminate-instances. One function, no constant, removes a term measured at AUC 0.53 / 0.51 / 0.35 that votes for the merge on 249 of 312 known-different same-label pairs. It must land BEFORE the association ordering fix is measured: today the attribute channel votes +1.13 median for exactly the neighbours that fix touches.
 1c. covisibility-hard-veto. Restores the rule the same method already states for every other channel. Effect on outcomes today is 0 of 41, so it is cheap; it also ships total_if_unvetoed, which the later ruling on the 0.30 overlap bar will need.
 1d. keeper-corruption-on-apply. Must land BEFORE persistence, because persistence is the change that first makes the merge apply block execute — 0 merges have been applied in any bundle under the current source. Landing it after would mean the first real merges drop sightings and freeze the survivor's centre.
 1e. assoc-locality-gap (ordering only, 2 of 119 adds) and merge-pending (0 measured effect). Lowest value; land them last or defer. Do NOT widen association_margin_m and do NOT touch the same-cycle veto.

STEP 2 — THE ONE EXPERIMENT (below), run on the tree from step 1.

STEP 3 — the TUNING CHANGES, each behind its own number from step 2, none before:
 3a. persistence-unreachable. Ships with merge.periodic_interval_s = 0.0. The interval is set only from the fresh-fraction measurement. DEPENDS ON 1d (the apply block) and on an owner ruling on the two apply-block defects; it also depends on 1a and 1b to have anything worth committing. Do not change merge_min_consecutive in the same change.
 3b. overlap-is-the-only-positive-channel. Ships inert at cap 0.0. DEPENDS ON 1a (self-scale) and on a ground-truth fit of the two 2D-overlap distributions before the cap leaves 0.0.

DEPENDENCY SUMMARY: 1a before 3b. 1b before measuring 1e. 1d before 3a. Step 0 before judging anything. Two fixes interact and must be measured together, not one after the other: the restored 1.0 m tracking fallback (1a) and the association candidate ordering (1e) both change what reaches the same accept decision, which fact A measures at 0.24 recall and 54 duplicate adds out of 119 calls.
plan.refuted:
same-cycle-veto-manufactures-duplicates — REFUTED by both lenses. The veto fires (7 of 119 adds on GA-493, 14 of 171 across three runs) but never on detector over-segmentation: 0 of 92 same-label same-cycle detection pairs in GA-493 intersect at all (max 3D IoU 0.000), and ground truth assigns the two sides of 15 of 15 blocked pairs to DIFFERENT real objects, including one unambiguous case (pillow_54 at IoU 0.859 versus pillow_53 at IoU 0.762, 0.051 m apart). It contributes 0 of 119 adds to the association loss. It is the guard a wider gap gate would need, not a defect. Do not re-open it.
Widening the 0.3 m association gap gate — REFUTED. 58 of 59 ground-truth re-observation adds already had their partner within 0.3 m (median 0.000 m, p90 0.09 m, max 0.46 m); the gate refused 1 of 59 and 0 of the 24 that survive an IoU >= 0.10 floor. The 32-34 of 86 far same-label neighbours are different instances of one kind (bimodal gap: median 0.10 m against p90 4.02 m). The hypothesis's own falsifier also fails: the fused box moves in-reach only from 52 to 54 of 86, the union box rescues 0 of 119.
merge_pending.json costing merges — REFUTED. The file is stale (4 of 4 bundles), but no recorded run ever read the count in a way that changed behaviour: 0 of 5 feed_stats.json carry the settle keys, no log holds the settle line, 5 of 5 runs are single-floor so the only branch acting on the count was unreachable. It explains 0 of the 3 held pairs and 0 of the 55 association duplicates.
"Only ONE positive channel" — corrected, not refuted. There are two (overlap and attributes); attributes is capped at 2.000 against a 2.9957 threshold, so overlap is still necessary on 97 of 97 rows. The arithmetic-impossibility boundary is V_larger > V_map / 2.71, not V_map / 20, and it was reached on 1 of 53 intersecting rows.
"Observations are the sole input to the association centroid" — FALSE. association.py:1247-1255 is a three-way precedence and an explicit centroid wins, which both call sites pass. Observations feed the covariance, the appearance descriptors and co-visibility — three consumers, not four.
The self-scale reach_m falsifier — WITHDRAWN. It fires on 16 of 40 pairs for an unrelated reason (the box at sweep time is not the box persisted at the end); the covariance can contribute at most 0.213 mm.
The merge-apply falsifier ("read merged_bbox from a merge row") — NOT RUNNABLE. All 15 GA-493 merge rows carry 10 keys and none is merged_bbox or bbox_source, and the DGX 144-stop bundle it names is not on this machine.
merge_min_consecutive = 2 buying precision — UNMEASURABLE, not measured at zero. No pair was ever scored above the threshold on a sweep that had a successor sweep, so the denominator is 0.

critic:
## Completeness gaps

**1. Nobody read the candidate generator's own exclusion log — the merge denominator is missing its other half.**
`/DATA/GRAPH-API/.claude/worktrees/found-merge-algorithm/lost3dsg/src/perception_module/association.py:994-1048` (`generate_candidates`) returns `(offered, excluded)`, and the runs record the excluded count. In `/home/xps/graphapi_ws/results/20260914_180343_hm3d_00824/hook_decisions.jsonl` there are 2 `not_offered_summary` rows: 16 pairs and 116 pairs, **100% for reason "outside the combined covariance shell"**. Run `20260914_174342` has 1 more. The plan states every merge rate over "116 distinct offered pairs" and never once states that a comparable number of pairs was never offered, nor whether any ground-truth duplicate is among them. The exclusion reason is the same collapsed covariance the plan is repairing, so this is not a side channel — it is the first stage of the same defect.
*Closer:* add the pair ids to the `not_offered_summary` row (additive key, `object_services.py:1773-1790`), then join against the GT duplicate list and publish merge recall through the whole funnel: offered → room gate → geometry gate → scored → streak → applied.

**2. Every merge number in the plan was measured on a tree that no longer exists.**
Commit `13d75b5` (the F1/F2 association fixes) landed at **2026-09-14 18:54:20 +0200**. Both evidence bundles predate it: `20260914_174342` and `20260914_180343`. Both still carry `observation_discard` rows with `"reason": "manager_motion_gate"` — 19 and 13 rows — which is precisely the gate F1 deleted. So the 97 scored rows, the 41-of-41 separation floor, the 116 pairs and the 3-of-3 streak refusals all describe a map built from fewer accepted detections than the current tree produces. The plan presents them as the current behaviour and its "one experiment" measures deltas against them.
*Closer:* re-run both scenes on HEAD **before** any step-1 fix lands. That baseline, not the pre-fix bundles, is what step 2's deltas mean.

**3. Unread path: the hypothesis garbage collector couples persistence to candidate generation.**
`_hypothesis_gc` at `/DATA/GRAPH-API/.claude/worktrees/found-merge-algorithm/lost3dsg/src/perception_module/object_services.py:1568-1578` deletes every hypothesis whose key is not in `live_keys` for this sweep. Candidates are regenerated each sweep from the covariance shell. A pair offered on sweep *n* only through the `gap_ok` branch (`association.py:1020-1024`) and not offered on sweep *n+1* loses its whole hypothesis, streak included. The persistence hypothesis blames sweep cadence alone; adding `merge.periodic_interval_s` cannot build a streak for a pair that is not re-offered. The covisibility hypothesis noticed this GC; the persistence one did not use it.
*Closer:* record, per sweep, the offered-pair set and the already-computed `dropped` count (`object_services.py:1828`), and report the fraction of pairs offered on two consecutive sweeps. That fraction, not the interval, is the ceiling on `merge_min_consecutive = 2`.

**4. The self-scale fix has an unnamed blast radius: it widens candidate generation.**
`search_radius` (`association.py:969-991`) returns `reach + sqrt(CHI2_99_3DOF * lambda_max(Sigma))`. At the collapsed covariance that term is ~0.0002 m; with real per-frame sighting centres (fix E2) it becomes a real shell. Offered pairs grow in an O(n²) loop over 104 objects (5,356 unordered pairs), and with them the hypothesis store, the per-pair scoring cost and the sweep duration. The plan names exactly one newly exposed path (the 64-sighting cap in covisibility) and misses this one.
